brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: Five hex base pieces: full bases at (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), (0,-1) and a half-e base at (-1,0), plus a half-n base at (-1,-1) supporting the drawer. Joint bolts at (0,0), (0,1), (0,-1) and (-1,0) lock the group together; check_build reports no loose-body warnings.

Three bins drop into cells and hang on their rims: bin:0,0,0 (full depth, 3 compartments), bin:0,1,0 (full depth, 2 compartments), bin:0,-1,0 (full depth, plain). Bins are not fixed to the base, so they can be lifted out.
drawer:0#-1,-1#cut sits on the cut face of the half-n base at (-1,-1).
handle:1,0,0;top mounted on the top cover cover:1,0,0;full;top, with inserts. Cover and handle meshes clear.

Fit is verified (meshClash clear, no errors), but this check does not assess weight or strength, so portability is only shown by having a handle and a compact footprint of about 7 cells, not verified as a load rating.

finish.summary: The build is a compact hex-base organizer with three removable bins (one 3-compartment, one 2-compartment, one plain), one drawer on a half base, and a top carry handle on a cover. check_build shows no errors and meshClash is clear. Remaining info note is only about open cap faces, which are optional. Strength and weight were not evaluated.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
